newsitem.title: INDIA: India eyes sunflower as palm olein prices rise.
newsitem.headline: India eyes sunflower as palm olein prices rise.

text.p: A rise in Malaysian palm olein prices has forced Indian edible oil traders to turn to cheaper U.S. and Argentine sunflower oil, imports of which will more than double this year, industry officials said on Wednesday.

"Indian importers are preferring sunflower oil as they are getting it cheaper compared to Malaysian palm olein," O.P. Goenka, president of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT), told Reuters.
"The U.S. and Argentina are the major suppliers," he said.
Goenka said India was importing Malaysian palm olein at around $620 CIF compared to $600 quoted for sunflower oil imports from the United States and Argentina.

Industry officials said Indian importers had signed contracts to import around 150,000 tonnes of sunflower for shipment between January and March compared to 60,000 tonnes of palm olein for the same period.
"I expect sunflower imports to be around 250,000 tonnes during 1996/97 (November-October)," Goenka said.
India imported 110,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in 1995/96.
Goenka said Malaysian palm olein prices had gone up mainly due to a surge in demand from China and Pakistan.
"Already 20,000 tonnes of sunflower oil has reached India ports, of which 10,000 tonnes was unloaded last week," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, said.
"Every week, nearly 5,000 tonnes of Malaysian palm olein is also arriving," Shah told.

Industry officials said groundnut oil prices had slightly eased in domestic markets during the past week due to increased import arrivals. It was quoted at around 34,300 rupees per tonne against 35,000 rupees last week.
"Groundnut oil prices have fallen because buyers are preferring cheaper edible oils like sunflower and palm olein," Shah said.
Shah said sunflower oil (crude) was quoted at 27,800 rupees per tonne compared to 29,000 rupees last week. "Prices have gone down because of import arrivals."
Palm olein was quoted at around 28,200 rupees per tonne compared to 29,000 last week.
Goenka said domestic edible oil arrivals were good and production was expected to be around 6.7 million tonnes, nearly the same as last year.
"But imports are going to rise to 1.5 million tonnes from last year's purchases of 1.15 million due to the rise in population and the increase in per capita income," Goenka said.
Shah said around 100 tonnes of groundnut oil was arriving in Bombay markets, the same as last week.
About 30,000 bags of soybean were arriving per day compared to 50,000 bags last week in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry, he added.
